tasks.title: Verify the scheduled-jobs story against django.tasks gaps
tasks.endGoal: The project has a demonstrated, documented pattern for recurring and delayed work: deadline-as-data (e.g. expires_at) + an idempotent sweep management command that goes through services; a cadence trigger per environment (local = manual/compose loop, prod = external scheduler); a cleanup command that prunes finished task-result rows.
tips: django.tasks core (Django 6.0) provides API only - NO worker, NO retries, NO delayed execution (run_after absent from core), NO periodic tasks, NO delivery guarantees, NO monitoring dashboard. Each gap needs a named owner in this repo.
Worker = the django-tasks reference package's DB backend + db_worker (`just worker`); in prod it is a separate long-running service deployed in lockstep with web so task code never drifts.

Sweep pattern (decided 2026-07-18): never schedule one event per row - store the deadline on the model, filter reads on it so correctness never depends on the scheduler, and let a frequent idempotent sweep materialize the state. Side-effectful closes go row-by-row through the owning service, not bulk update().
Sweep commands live in apps/<app>/management/commands (layering: management -> services); recurring cadence changes are infrastructure-only edits, new jobs = new command + new schedule entry.
JSON-only task args (tuples become lists, no datetimes/models) - the existing pk-strings rule already complies; keep return values JSON-safe or return nothing.
No timeouts / rate limits / uniqueness in the framework: guard in the task body (select_for_update, status checks) where duplicate or hung execution would hurt.
